summary: Feed s143_double is degraded: 21.5% of TCP sessions are one-way and 58.0% of frames remain VXLAN-encapsulated, preventing IDS stateful inspection and payload analysis.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/TAP aggregation is delivering only one direction for many flows. 41 of 191 TCP sessions (21.5%) show single direction, typical of asymmetric routing with single-sided SPAN/TAP or flow-based load-balancing that splits client->server and server->client across different tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly and stateful signatures. One-way sessions cannot be reassembled, handshakes fail, and bidirectional attack detection is blind, causing missed intrusions and inaccurate state tracking.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each 5-tuple to the same IDS port so the IDS sees complete handshakes and can reassemble streams for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding overlay traffic without decapsulation. 1515 of 2610 frames (58.0%) arrive inside VXLAN tunnel, indicating strip/decapsulation policy is missing or not applied to this feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS sees only outer VXLAN/UDP/IP headers and cannot parse inner Ethernet/IP/TCP payload. Signatures and protocol decoders fail on 58% of traffic, leaving overlay workloads effectively unmonitored.

recommended_fix.why: Strip VXLAN headers at the packet broker to expose inner frames to the IDS for full L2-L7 inspection and signature matching.
